_what_this_is: A SYNTHETIC stage-1 market artifact, so the commercial loop can be
demonstrated without a live Census or FMCSA call. Every business named
below is invented. No row here came from a public register, and nothing
in it should be presented as a real company or a real observation.
It exists because the loop refused to run at all without an artifact, and
no sample was committed -- so the Market -> Growth -> Marketing -> customer
-> load -> margin story, which is the whole commercial argument, could not
be shown from a clean checkout. The honest answer to 'no artifact' was an
empty Growth page, and an empty page is not a demo.
THE RIGHTS SEMANTICS ARE REAL, and are the point of the fixture. Two
sources: one public register that does NOT license outreach, and one
first-party list that does. The loop must refuse to market to the first
and allow the second. Changing permits_direct_marketing to true on the
register would make this fixture a lie AND make the demo prove nothing.

identity_strength uses the vocabulary commercial_prospects_identity_ck accepts: NAMED_ONLY, ADDRESS_MATCHED, VERIFIED, SELF_IDENTIFIED. A first draft of this fixture said CORROBORATED -- a word from the authority ladder that this column does not take -- and the database refused the insert, which is the constraint doing exactly its job.

ORDER MATTERS. demo_commercial_loop.py takes candidates[0] and files it under a PUBLIC_REGISTER source, because demonstrating the outreach refusal is the point of that step. The register-sourced candidate is therefore first here; with them the other way round the page labelled an inbound enquiry 'no outreach licence', which is the wrong story and a fixture contradicting itself on screen.
